set_by: user, explicitly, for the overnight window
why: MOP owns the heavy machine overnight. It already holds most of 28 cores and the GPU. Anything heavy run beside it would both compete with it and produce timings too contaminated to mean anything.
forbidden_while_this_mode_is_active: loading or serving the 92 GB flagship artifact
full corpus embedding or large retrieval index builds
real Fabric throughput or latency benchmarking
allowed: small deterministic fixtures and unit tests
data acquisition, hashing, licensing, splits, dedup boundaries
proof and search scaffolding against toy theorems
HIDE Context OS, tool/effect registry, Bridge events, Fabric simulator, adapter registry, CLI and schema generation, migrations, documentation inventory

cpu_policy.note: launchd ProcessType Background pins a heavy job to a flat ~1 core and is the wrong lever for throughput, but it is the right lever here: the goal tonight is to stay out of MOP's way, not to go fast.

standing_refusals_that_are_not_part_of_t.ODYSSEY_LAUNCH_AUTHORIZED: false, and independently refused by the substrate capability gate. This is NOT a resource-mode restriction and does not lift when the mode does.

how_to_lift: Change mode here and say who decided. Lifting this mode does not authorize Odyssey: that needs a substrate with capability_verdict APPROVED in odyssey/launch/SUBSTRATE_CAPABILITY.json, which no artifact currently has.
the_one_thing_worth_a_heavy_window_when_: Representation escalation. It is the only genuinely blocked question -- what representation replaces the semantically collapsed sub-bit artifact. Preregistered in HAWKING_REPRESENTATION_ESCALATION_TOURNAMENT.json so the design is fixed before any compute is spent on it.
